tools.name: answer_inquiry
tools.description: Answers the open question (Rückfrage) about an ordered certificate with the customer's answers: values keyed by the item keys get_status listed, files the question asks for, and an explanation. Ask the customer first and send only what they confirmed.

tools.name: check_eligibility
tools.description: Checks whether Energieausweis Express can issue a Verbrauchsausweis (consumption-based energy certificate) for a residential building in Germany, before any order exists. tools.description: Finds the building at a German address in our 3D building data. Returns the building at the address first, then nearby buildings, each with a building_ref for start_order and a short German description (type, storeys, footprint). tools.name: get_certificate
tools.description: Returns download links for the issued certificate and its invoice (PDF). The links work for one hour and open nothing else, so they can be shown to the user; call again for fresh ones. The customer also got both by email. Changes nothing.

tools.name: get_listing_facts
tools.description: Returns what a property listing must state about the energy certificate (§ 87 GEG): type of certificate, Endenergieverbrauch, main energy carrier of the heating, year built and Effizienzklasse, as ready-to-paste German text. Only once the certificate is issued. Changes nothing.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Shows where the order stands, in plain German words: prepared, ordered, being checked by the Energieberater, waiting for an answer to a Rückfrage (with its questions), issued. Changes nothing.

tools.name: request_confirmation
tools.description: Sends the customer one email with a link to their prepared order on our website. This does NOT order or charge anything: the customer checks the data there, adds what is missing (usually photos of the street side and the heating) and orders and pays on our page themselves. tools.name: review_order
tools.description: Shows the order's data and what it still needs before the customer can order: the open points (which field to send, and in German why), whether a Verbrauchsausweis is possible, the price, and a preliminary result once the consumption is complete. Changes nothing.

tools.description: Starts a draft order for the building the user confirmed (building_ref from find_building). Orders and charges nothing. findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "request_confirmation" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "update_order" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: add_document, check_eligibility, get_certificate, request_confirmation, review_order · Private data: add_document, answer_inquiry, start_order · Public sink: add_document, answer_inquiry, get_certificate, request_confirmation, review_order, update_order.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: add_document, check_eligibility, get_certificate, request_confirmation, review_order · Private data: add_document, answer_inquiry, start_order · Public sink: add_document, answer_inquiry, get_certificate, request_confirmation, review_order, update_order

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
